detail: The distractor note says (x - 5)(x^2 + 4) gives '-4x - 20 instead of -4x + 20' when expanded, but it expands to x^3 - 5x^2 + 4x - 20, so the x-term is +4x (and the constant -20); the stated expansion is wrong math. Key B is correct.

fix.old: (x - 5)(x^2 + 4) factors -4 out of the second group as +4, giving -4x - 20 instead of -4x + 20 when expanded;
fix.new: (x - 5)(x^2 + 4) factors -4 out of the second group as +4, so it expands to x^3 - 5x^2 + 4x - 20, with +4x - 20 in place of -4x + 20;

detail: Choice 768π has no coherent mistake behind it: the byHand note '768π uses r^2 · r in place of r^3 wrongly (4/3 · 576)' is not a real error (r^2 · r is r^3), and 768 = (4/3)(576) matches no natural slip. Replacing it with 192π = (4/3)π(12)^2 (squares the radius instead of cubing it) gives a genuine distractor; reordered ascending, the key stays D. byHand must be updated to match (see separate finding).

detail: Desmos reserves r for polar graphs, so 'r=\sqrt{\frac{720}{5}}' graphs a polar circle instead of defining a variable, and the next line \frac{4}{3}r^3 will not evaluate to 2304. (Item geo-salt-pile-cone-circumference warns about exactly this.) Use another letter.
The byHand distractor list contains raw LaTeX (-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}, \sqrt{3}) instead of the plain-text math used everywhere else in byHand, so it will render as source code.

fix.old: Distractors: -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} divides cosine by sine (the cotangent); \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} is the cotangent with the quadrant II sign lost; \sqrt{3} is tan(π/3), the reference-angle value with the sign lost.
fix.new: Distractors: -√3/3 divides cosine by sine (the cotangent); √3/3 is the cotangent with the quadrant II sign lost; √3 is tan(π/3), the reference-angle value with the sign lost.
